ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the area of square $ABCD$ is $100 \text{cm}^2$. Triangle $\triangle ABP$ is a right-angled triangle with $\angle P = 90^\circ$, and $PB = 6\text{cm}$. What is the length of $AP$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that the area of square ABCD is $100\,\text{cm}^{2}$,\\
it follows that AB=10cm,\\
since \(\triangle\)ABP is a right triangle with \(\angle P=90^\circ\) and PB=6cm,\\
therefore AP=$\sqrt{AB^{2}-BP^{2}}=\sqrt{10^{2}-6^{2}}=\boxed{8}\,\text{cm}$.
